newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Ivorian 97/98 cocoa 1.1 mln tonnes- B.Callebaut.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian 97/98 cocoa 1.1 mln tonnes- B.Callebaut.

text.p: The chief executive office of Barry Callebaut said on Thursday his company estimated the 1997/1998 Ivorian Coast's cocoa crop at 1.1 million tonnes.
"It will be 1.1 million," Pierre Vermaut told Reuters after a news conference. His company estimates the crop during the current 1996/1997 season at 1.14 million tonnes, he said.
Vermaut estimated Ghana's cocoa crop at 330,000 tonnes in 1996/97 and said he expected the harvest to remain steady in 1997/98.
"I don't see why it should be different in Ghana," he said.
Vermaut also projected the Indonesian cocoa crop at 330,000 tonnes in 1996/97 and 10 percent higher in 1997/98.
"Indonesia is still growing. I would guess 10 percent more in 1997/98. They're still planting," he said.

Barry Callebaut, the group formed by the merger of France's Cacao Barry and Swiss Callebaut AG, is the world's largest cocoa bean processor and a major force in the finished chocolate and chocolate coatings market. It operates 19 plants worldwide, including three cocoa bean processing plants in Ivory Coast.
